microtheory.name: music_history_styles
microtheory.definition: Historical periods + genres + style markers in Western (and selected other) music. Medieval, Renaissance, Baroque, Classical, Romantic, Modern, plus jazz, blues, rock, electronic, world. Substrate analogue: stylistic priors the substrate can apply when listening — different scales, rhythms, harmonic vocabularies.

concepts.name: medieval_music
concepts.definition: ~500-1400 CE. Modal scales (not yet major/minor). Plainchant, organum, motet. Substrate analogue: substrate's modal pitch priors.

concepts.name: renaissance_music
concepts.definition: 1400-1600. Polyphony fully developed. Palestrina, Lassus. Modal still but transitioning. Substrate analogue: substrate's parallel-voice tracking emphasis.

concepts.name: baroque_music
concepts.definition: 1600-1750. Tonality established. Bach, Handel. Counterpoint mastery. Concerto, fugue, suite. Substrate analogue: substrate's tonal-hierarchy framework.

concepts.name: classical_music_period
concepts.definition: 1750-1820. Mozart, Haydn, early Beethoven. Sonata form, clarity, balance. Substrate analogue: substrate's hierarchical-form template.

concepts.name: romantic_music
concepts.definition: 1820-1900. Brahms, Wagner, Liszt, Mahler. Expanded harmony, expressive freedom, larger forces. Substrate analogue: substrate's extended-harmonic vocabulary.

concepts.name: 20th_century_classical
concepts.definition: 1900-2000. Diverse — impressionism (Debussy), serialism (Schoenberg), minimalism (Reich), avant-garde (Cage). Substrate analogue: substrate's pluralistic-pattern recognition.

concepts.name: blues
concepts.definition: African-American origins, 12-bar structure, blue notes, call-and-response. Foundation of rock + jazz. Substrate analogue: substrate's specific scale + harmonic template.

concepts.name: jazz
concepts.definition: Improvised, swung rhythm, extended chords, blues influence. Bebop, cool, modal, fusion subgenres. Substrate analogue: substrate's improvisation framework over chord progressions.

concepts.name: rock
concepts.definition: Loud, electric, drum-driven. Pentatonic + power chords. Verse-chorus form. Substrate analogue: substrate's energy-rhythm template.

concepts.name: electronic_music
concepts.definition: Synthesizers + drum machines + samplers as primary instruments. House, techno, ambient. Substrate analogue: substrate's synthesized-sound framework.

concepts.name: hip_hop
concepts.definition: Sampling, beats, rapping. Beat + flow as central elements. Substrate analogue: substrate's rhythm + speech-tone interleaved structure.

concepts.name: folk
concepts.definition: Traditional music transmitted orally. Often modal, strophic, narrative. Substrate analogue: substrate's transmitted-tradition pattern.

concepts.name: world_music
concepts.definition: Music traditions outside Western mainstream. Indian classical (ragas), gamelan, flamenco, African polyrhythm. Substrate analogue: substrate's non-Western scale + rhythm priors.

concepts.name: indian_classical_music
concepts.definition: Raga + tala system. Microtonal pitches, complex rhythmic cycles. Substrate analogue: substrate's microtonal + complex-meter capabilities.

concepts.name: gamelan
concepts.definition: Indonesian percussion ensemble. Unique tuning systems (slendro, pelog). Substrate analogue: substrate's per-tradition tuning prior.

concepts.name: flamenco
concepts.definition: Spanish guitar + voice + dance. Phrygian-dominant scale. Compás (cyclic rhythm). Substrate analogue: substrate's specific scale + rhythm cycle.

concepts.name: african_polyrhythm
concepts.definition: Multi-layer interlocking rhythmic patterns. Many West African traditions. Substrate analogue: substrate's multi-stream rhythm.

concepts.name: key_personality
concepts.definition: Different keys historically associated with different moods (D major = triumphant, B♭ minor = funereal). Largely cultural/instrumental in origin. Substrate analogue: substrate's per-key affective association.

concepts.name: musical_period_style_markers
concepts.definition: Each historical period has identifiable harmonic + rhythmic + formal conventions. Listeners can date music to ±50 years. Substrate analogue: substrate's stylistic-classification feature space.

concepts.name: musical_idiom
concepts.definition: Stable feature combinations marking a specific style — blues idiom, jazz idiom, etc. Substrate analogue: substrate's style-Mt.

concepts.name: musical_borrowing
concepts.definition: Use of material from another tradition. Cross-cultural fusion + appropriation. Substrate analogue: substrate's cross-Mt pattern transfer.

concepts.name: performance_practice
concepts.definition: Historically-informed performance: original instruments + period conventions. HIP movement. Substrate analogue: substrate's era-specific reproduction parameters.

concepts.name: improvisation
concepts.definition: Real-time musical creation within stylistic framework. Jazz, baroque, Indian classical. Substrate analogue: substrate's constrained generation over learned patterns.

concepts.name: notation_evolution
concepts.definition: From neumes (medieval) → modern staff. Different traditions: tablature, lead sheets, graphic scores. Substrate analogue: substrate's notation-encoding conventions.

rules.name: style_priors_shape_perception
rules.head: the substrate is in a known musical style context
rules.body: stylistic priors (scale, rhythm, harmonic vocabulary) bias its expectations. Substrate's per-style Mt activation.

rules.name: cross_cultural_listening_requires_prior_switching
rules.head: the substrate processes music from an unfamiliar tradition
rules.body: its Western priors may distort perception unless explicitly switched to the tradition's priors. Substrate's per-tradition Mt selection.

rules.name: period_markers_enable_dating
rules.head: the substrate identifies historical period markers
rules.body: harmonic + rhythmic + formal features narrow the time of composition. Substrate's classification by feature.

rules.name: improvisation_is_generation_within_constraints
rules.head: the substrate produces music in a style with improvisation tradition
rules.body: generation operates within stylistic Mt constraints — scale, rhythm template, harmonic progression. Substrate's constrained-generation pattern.
